questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A crucial aspect for me was that the destination was an English speaking country. Second, I have always been intrigued by the UK. I wanted to experience living in a British culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The experience overall was amazing. Probably the best time I have had in my life!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I just had to check up on my emails quite often which could take a bit of time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction day for all the exchange students, although most information and assistance I had was through email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through my host institution. Only offer off campus accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most graduates and thirds year students live off campus. On campus is mostly first year students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a form for you to fill out and then you needed to upload a picture for your student card. pretty straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: IT support, support to manage stress, everyone was assigned a tutor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful! I got my first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Overall, it can seem confusing and overwhelming in the beginning, but it turns out fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses, I thought was fine. It was very different compared to back home, but after a couple of weeks you get an idea on how they want things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Style of teaching was pretty similar. (Lectures, workshops)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CNS and Cancer

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choose what you are interested in learning about.

questions.answer: I did some travelling through Europe.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transportation is extremely expensive in the UK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university have a lot of societies and sport activities. Som examples: swimming, dancing, basketball, soccer, salsa, golf etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you have interest in any sport, sign up. The sports facilities are amazing. For socialising join a society. They have a variety of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore UK. If you get the chance travel to other countries.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easier than expected. Everyone was so nice and welcoming. Very easy to talk to people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just reach out and introduce yourself as an exchange student. Worked for me.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People being kind and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. One big campus with all sorts of studies, compared to back home where it is spread in different places.
2. People are amazingly friendly
3. Teachers are nice and helpful. They want you to do good!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have the full responsibility to reach out and sort everything out. No one is doing it for you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having an amazing supervisor, who helped me with the academic stuff a lot, and making friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the way of teaching and learning as it was different from back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, I definitely do not regret the decision of doing an exchange and will definitely do it again if the opportunity arrives.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
